Exploring the eﬀects of gravity on a coﬂow 
diﬀusion ﬂame in an electric ﬁeld

Electric Field Effects
Ion reactions make up a small subset of 
combustion kinetics.
Microscopic electric field effects:
• Charge separation
•Acceleration prevented by                     collisions 
with neutrals
• ~100 m/s ion drift velocity
Macroscopic field effects:
• Ion-driven wind (~1 m/s)
• Reshaping of the reaction zone
• Change in flame luminosity
• Altered stability
• Forced extinction
Starik and Titova, 2002

Flames and Body Forces
Instead of the classic teardrop shape, low-g flames 
tend to exhibit a more spherical shape, owing to the 
lack of buoyancy.
Effects of ion-driven convection are physically similar 
to buoyancy.
Using both, the NASA 2.2-s 
Drop Tower and the ISS 
(proposed), we will study the 
influence of chemi-ionization on 
combustion without buoyancy.

Normal and Low Gravity Results (NASA)

Conclusions and Future Work
• Flame oscillations are present for a variety of applied field strengths.
• Field driven oscillations can be arranged into two regimes: 
• Those which cause visible flame movement (~10 - 20Hz)
• Luminous oscillations (~30 - 40Hz region)
• Lower coflow velocities are necessary to recognize the contribution of buoyancy to 
ionization.
